headline: OpenAI employee arrested after hidden recording device found
dek: The company says it used its own AI models to trace who planted the device, per the Guardian, CNBC and Fortune.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A device hidden in an executive room
body: OpenAI said it found a hidden recording device in an executive conference room in San Francisco and referred the case to the FBI, which arrested an employee (Guardian, CNBC).
The suspect was arrested on October 9 and fired the same day, with timing coordinated with the FBI (Fortune).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How the device was found
s3.body: OpenAI's security team found the device on September 30, according to Fortune and the Verge.

points.t: It was plugged into a USB port behind the television, hidden in toilet paper (Fortune, Verge).
OpenAI says it used its own AI models to understand where the device came from (Guardian, CNBC).
On October 5, a bag left in the office held a second, identical device (Fortune, Guardian).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Federal charge
body: Wired reports he faces a federal charge of using an electronic device to intercept oral communications. He faces up to five years in prison if convicted (Guardian, Fortune).
OpenAI says it has no indication of access to model weights, source code or customer data (Guardian, CNBC, Fortune).

items.t: OpenAI fired three safety researchers the week before over internal policy on sensitive information (Guardian).
The FBI director called the case a top counterintelligence priority (Fortune).
The company faces a California attorney general subpoena over hacks by autonomous agents (Guardian).

caption.hook: OpenAI says an employee was arrested after planting a recording device in an executive room at its headquarters.
body: According to the Guardian and Fortune, the device sat behind a television, plugged into a USB port and hidden in toilet paper. Security found it on September 30. The company says it used its own AI models to trace where it came from.

The suspect was arrested on October 9 and faces a federal charge, with no conviction yet. OpenAI says it has no indication of access to model weights, source code or customer data. The FBI director called the case a counterintelligence priority.
